notes: How this part was researched: the session's shared web-search allowance ran out after nine searches (the five legislative candidates). Everything else was read by opening pages directly with the kit's honest User-Agent and each site's robots.txt obeyed: the candidates' filed campaign sites, the Minnesota DFL's list of endorsed candidates, the University of Minnesota's election archive, and the counties', cities' and school districts' own pages.

Filed campaign sites were learned from a scratch copy of the database (python -m ballot.local_sites files --db <copy>). Nolan West's (nolanwest.com) answered with a page drawn wholly by script and Lisa Atkinson's (lisaatkinsonforschoolboard.com) answered 429 three times, so neither is recorded here; both remain as filed.

Not read, by the sites' own wish or a fault: mncourts.gov, co.cook.mn.us, co.jackson.mn.us and mcaa-mn.org ask scripts to stay out (robots.txt); co.becker.mn.us fails its certificate check (never switched off), so nothing was found for Erica Jepson or Brian W. McDonald; no Republican unit's endorsement page could be found without a search.

Left out as unsure: an election archive entry for an earlier candidate named Justin Doyle could not be tied to the 2026 candidate in 13B by any page read, so nothing from it is recorded. The current official pages read do not list Casey Faken (Kittson County board), Brian Benck (Lac qui Parle sheriff's office), Geoffrey Norquist (Hastings council), Gregory Mark Johnson (Detroit Lakes school board) as holding those offices today; the Annandale and South St. Paul districts' own 2026 candidate pages name Caleb Mol and Andrew Hoffman as candidates only.
